blocks.text: ISO/IEC 42001 specifies requirements for establishing, implementing, maintaining
An effective AIMS connects organizational objectives, responsible-use principles, AI system inventory, risk
Support may include:
AI Context and Scope
Define organizational roles, AI activities, systems, services, stakeholders and AIMS boundaries
AI Governance
Establish policies, responsibilities, decision-making, accountability and oversight
AI System Inventory
Document relevant AI systems, purpose, ownership, lifecycle status, data and dependencies
Risk and Impact Assessment
Identify risks and potential impacts to the organization, individuals and other stakeholders
Lifecycle Controls
Address design, acquisition, development, deployment, operation, monitoring, change
Data and Third-Party Governance
Review data quality, provenance, suppliers, external models and service dependencies
Transparency and Responsible Use
Establish appropriate information, human oversight, instructions and use limitations
Performance and Certification Readiness
Support monitoring, internal audit, management review, corrective action
1. AI Discovery and Scoping
Understand AI systems, use cases, roles, data, stakeholders, risks and certification objectives
2. Gap and Maturity Assessment
Evaluate existing AI governance, risk, development and oversight practices
3. Governance and Program Planning
Define policy, responsibilities, objectives, risk methodology and implementation roadmap
4. AI Risk and Impact Assessment
Assess priority systems and define proportionate treatment and oversight
5. Control and Process Implementation
Develop lifecycle, data, supplier, transparency, monitoring and incident processes
6. Stakeholder Enablement
Train system owners, developers, users, procurement, legal, risk and leadership roles
7. Internal Audit and Management Review
Evaluate the AIMS and support leadership review and corrective action
8. Certification Coordination and Maintenance
Support independent audit preparation and ongoing AIMS operation
